headline: Prototypes of the French Thundart Multiple Launch Rocket System (MLRS) will undergo testing in Ukraine. The system is being developed by MBDA and Safran to replace the aging M270 LRU (Lance-Roquettes Unitaire), the French variant of the American M270. The Thundart's rockets are compatible with the M270 LRU, although their full specifications have not yet been disclosed. The only confirmed detail is a range of 150 km, with plans to increase it to 500 km in the future. Safran is expected to integrate the same guidance system used in the AASM Hammer family of precision-guided air-to-ground bombs into the rocket. The launcher is mounted on a Scania 8×8 truck chassis equipped with a rotating launcher mount.

headline: Iraqi security forces have foiled a sabotage attempt targeting the Badra Oil Field, where Russia's Gazprom Neft holds a 30% stake. Officials said a suspect was arrested after security forces discovered an improvised explosive device (IED) inside his vehicle before any attack could be carried out. During questioning, the suspect confessed that he had been recruited through specialized job-search chat rooms and was acting under foreign direction in exchange for a $2,000 payment. Investigators said digital forensic evidence corroborated his account, including communications with a handler linked to a Ukrainian phone number. The investigation remains ongoing. If confirmed, the incident could indicate that, alongside its campaign against Russian oil refineries, Ukrainian intelligence is also expanding efforts to target Russian oil and gas interests outside the immediate region.

headline: The Houthis claimed responsibility overnight for striking two Saudi oil tankers, the "ENCELIA" and "LAYLA," with ballistic missiles and drones, part of a new blockade on Saudi Arabia. Saudi officials confirmed one tanker was hit near al-Shakiq. Dozens were killed in ground clashes between Houthi forces and Saudi-aligned Yemeni fighters in the A-Chale area of southern Yemen.
